Our central result is that retrieval metrics can rank memory policies backwards: a retention policy and its retain-everything control return the identical statement at rank 1 for every test query, yet differ by 29.5 and 65.6 points in reader accuracy on two readers when no date is shown. Contamination@5, the metric we add, ranks them correctly where current@1 and current@5 do not. Withdrawing the lexical anchor that statements carry costs deployed keying mechanisms tens of points of freshness; entity resolution on both the write path and the query recovers most of the loss. Three deployed systems (Mem0, Graphiti, LangMem) and a reimplemented ERASE each handle supersession differently, and no single scoring convention describes all four. We release the data, a frozen evaluator, and reference baselines.
Information Retrieval.comment: Accepted to Findings of EACL 2027. 39 pages, 3 figures. Code and data: https://github.com/thenexuslab/stalebench-release

Multimedia.title: Reveal: A Provenance-Aware System for Multimodal Urban Data Exploration
Multimedia.summary: Urban sensing initiatives increasingly produce multimodal datasets that combine visual and textual information to capture city characteristics and subjective factors such as safety, comfort, and accessibility. Yet, analyzing such data at scale remains difficult, as manual inspection is unfeasible and automated methods struggle to interpret subjective cues and uncover relationships across diverse data modalities. Moreover, existing workflows rarely make exploration steps explicit, hindering reproducibility. To address these challenges, we introduce Reveal, a provenance-aware visual analytics system for exploring heterogeneous urban data. Reveal enables users to build dataflows by combining text and image searches across coordinated views, chaining queries into pipelines, and applying set operations within an exploration diagram while capturing analytical provenance. We evaluate Reveal through two case studies focused on accessibility and walkability.
Multimedia.comment: Accepted to SIBGRAPI 2026

Multimedia.title: Streaming across viewing conditions - The effect of viewing distance and display luminance on video quality
Multimedia.summary: The visibility of streamed video distortions is affected by the user's display and viewing conditions, such as their display's luminance or the viewing distance. Distortions become less visible at lower luminance levels or farther viewing distances. However, most image and video quality metrics assume fixed optimal display and viewing conditions, making them insensitive to the viewing conditions. In this work, we demonstrate how existing metrics can be adapted to account for both factors and compare such an adaptation with the metrics that natively model viewing conditions. First, we collected a new video quality dataset, HDR-VDC, which contains streaming distortions in 4K HDR videos. The dataset consists of 12 4K and 4 FHD HDR source video content, each distorted with AV1 encoding and Lanczos upscaling from a lower resolution. The quality loss due to the distortions was measured at two viewing distances, corresponding to 60 and 120 pixels per visual degree, and two display mean luminance levels, varying by a factor of 8 in terms of luminance. Next, we developed a pre-processing framework that lets us adapt many quality metrics so that they can evaluate content across the viewing distances and luminance levels. The framework employs a display model and perceptually uniform encoding, PU21, to account for the effect of display luminance, and perspective projection scaling (PPS) to account for the effect of viewing distance. We used the framework to compare the performance of 35 state-of-the-art metrics. This allowed us to identify a selection of existing quality metrics that can be effectively adapted to account for the viewing conditions.

Multimedia.title: Sequential Semantic-Non-Semantic Watermarking: Robustness Against UnMarker Attacks
Multimedia.summary:
Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have accelerated digital content generation and intensified concerns around fraud, misuse, counterfeiting, and content provenance. Defensive image watermarking provides a practical mechanism for identifying and tracing digital content, but recent watermark-removal attacks challenge its robustness. This study investigates Sequential Semantic Non-Semantic Watermarking (SSNSW), which combines HiDDeN and StegaStamp as complementary non-semantic and semantic watermarking schemes. Using 50 images from MS-COCO and CelebA-HQ, both embedding orders are evaluated, followed by UnMarker's non-semantic and semantic attacks applied individually and sequentially.
  Results show that both watermarks remain highly decodable after dual embedding, with only limited embedding-order effects. Under individual attacks, one watermark generally remains strongly decodable: StegaStamp under the non-semantic attack and HiDDeN under the semantic attack. Sequential attacks are therefore required to substantially reduce both watermark signals, while attack order has a limited and configuration-dependent effect. The semantic attack also shows a broader effect across the two watermark types than the non-semantic attack. LPIPS remains relatively low in several settings, although qualitative inspection reveals noticeable distortions, particularly in selected facial images, indicating that LPIPS should not be used alone to assess visual quality.
  Overall, the findings show that combining complementary watermark types can increase robustness against single-stage removal attacks and motivate broader multi-layer watermarking, stronger perceptual evaluation, and further study of sequential watermark-removal strategies.
Multimedia.comment: 13 pages, 16 figures. Preprint based on M.Sc. thesis research

Multimedia.title: Equal Dose, Different Coverage:Tracing Rate and Duration in Image Editing
Multimedia.summary: Benchmarks for scientific image editing test whether a model draws the outcome of a described process, leaving open which representations carry its errors and whether correcting them yields the right quantity. We study this question with an airbrush of fixed deposition profile, under which exchanging rate and duration preserves the dose and should preserve the endpoint, yet changes the edited coverage. Matched-norm activation patches across text positions and denoising stages show that, in distilled FLUX with Chinese prompts, representations at unchanged text positions (context) carry this discrepancy: early context transfers 3.51 of the 3.98 percentage-point (pp) signed route difference, against 0.09 pp for equal-norm updates at the two changed digits. Early image latents transmit native (unpatched) route differences across two FLUX configurations and OmniGen, while text-position effects depend on configuration. The trace predicts an intervention: share early context between routes while each retains its own digits. On independent English layouts, this reduces the distilled-FLUX absolute route gap from 1.13 to 0.60 pp, outperforms early digit sharing, and improves agreement more than in base FLUX under directly paired tests. Calibrated evaluation, which prescribes an area for each dose, separates this gain from accuracy: sharing the full prompt encoding produces identical route images with target errors of 8-16 pp, and stating the target percentage directly retains a compressed area response. Localization predicts a consistency gain on new layouts, and calibration measures the quantity error that agreement leaves unresolved.

Multimedia.title: Appear2Meaning: A Cross-Cultural Benchmark for Structured Cultural Metadata Inference from Images
Multimedia.summary: Museum records express how people understand heritage objects through cultural and historical relations. Recovering these human attributions from images is a technical challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce Appear2Meaning, a cross-cultural benchmark of 750 museum objects for image-only recovery of title, culture, period, origin, and creator. Its evaluation framework distinguishes field-level from complete-record compatibility and uses human validation for semantic judgement. Across nine VLMs, mean field accuracy is 36.16--49.82%; 7.20--17.02% of records have all four contextual fields compatible, and 2.13--7.87% have all five, including title. For the two tested models, image-only input yields 12.6--32.2 percentage points higher reference compatibility for culture, period, and origin than a museum-and-title-only control.

Information Retrieval.title: User First Intelligence: Three Measurements of Search and AI-Answer Analytics (SEO and GEO/AEO), and a Knowledge-Graph Framework for Query Discovery Beyond Search Volume
Information Retrieval.summary: People say what they want to know in many places besides a search box, and the tools that search and AI-answer optimization (SEO and GEO/AEO) rely on see only part of that demand, through models reported as counts. This paper reports three measurements of such instruments and a framework. On the area-code section of a large US telecom provider's site, two commercial analytics platforms differed on estimated monthly visits by 7.5x to 27.1x (8.6x to 29.9x worldwide); across twelve sections of the domain the ratio ran from 0.20x to 7.24x with no detectable relation to section age, while they agreed on which section is larger in 60 of 66 pairs. On 37,193 reviews of 378 telecom stores linked to a 42,994-node keyword taxonomy, review demand and search volume agreed on branches to a varying degree (Spearman 0.47 to 0.75; 0.91 post hoc) and barely on topics (0.18), on links two blind AI annotators judged two-thirds correct; on the 372 area codes, a public count of Wikipedia requests for each code and vendor volume agreed roughly on ranking (0.45 over 240 articles, gone once keywords matched per code are held constant) and not on magnitudes, predictions fixed first. In one vendor's index of AI answers naming or citing the largest companies of each S&P 500 sector, of four predictions written first, one held, one in direction only and two failed; video and community sites took a median 21% of citation incidences on Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode against 0.6% to 9.2% on four other surfaces, in every sector, and in education answers in each of 13 countries read later. Estimates and sources need measuring per instrument and surface. User First Intelligence (UFI), built on that premise, collects what people ask beyond the website, links it to an industry ontology and scores where an organization does not answer; an open implementation is released, its score not evaluated. No causal claim is made.
Information Retrieval.comment: 43 pages, 10 figures. Preprint, not peer reviewed. Data and scripts in the ancillary files; implementation at https://github.com/VenkataPagadalaGIT/ufi

Information Retrieval.title: Fidelity Before Structure: Verbatim Chunks Beat Lossy Artifact Extraction in Long-Conversation LLM Memory
Information Retrieval.summary: A growing class of conversational-memory systems compresses dialogue history into structured artifacts (extracted facts, decisions, or events). The premise is that distilled structure retrieves better than raw text. We test this premise with a controlled ablation. Within one fixed retrieval--rerank--reasoning pipeline, we swap only the stored representation (LLM-extracted typed artifacts versus verbatim conversation chunks) and hold the model, retriever, reranker, and judge constant. Verbatim chunks win by 15.9 points on LoCoMo (43.9% vs. 28.0%) and by 22.0 points on LongMemEval-S (67.4% vs. 45.4%). A semantic graph does not recover the gap, and six confound controls reproduce the effect. The mechanism is lossy distillation rather than structure per se. Accuracy tracks how much source text survives in the store, and the extracted-artifact pipeline does not beat naive RAG in overall accuracy (chunks do abstain worse; see Limitations). For the extraction designs we test, structured memory should augment verbatim text rather than replace it. Adding artifacts alongside chunks costs no detected accuracy, while substituting them forfeits the gap. Code and data are available at https://github.com/tao-hpu/cog-canvas.
Information Retrieval.comment: v5: camera-ready version. Accepted to EACL 2027 (main conference). 39 pages, 6 figures. Code and data: https://github.com/tao-hpu/cog-canvas

Information Retrieval.title: From Evidence to Judgment: Trace-Augmented Reasoning under Conflicting Evidence
Information Retrieval.summary: Retrieved documents often disagree, contain outdated information, or fail to support any answer, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems have no reliable way to decide which documents to trust. We treat this as a reasoning problem and test it separately from answer generation. We release 943 training and validation examples and a disjoint 736-example benchmark, and fine-tune four language models to write a structured think trace before answering: the model judges each document, infers the conflict pattern, and writes a grounded answer or a justified refusal. Our evaluation framework, CATS (Conflict-Aware Trust Score), scores grounded refusal, behavioural adherence, factual grounding, and single-truth recall; a human study validates factual grounding and single-truth recall (kappa=0.78 and 0.79). The think trace improves the answer/refuse decision: under all three prompts, untuned models score at most 0.429 Refusal F1 (F1 with refusal as the positive class) and trace-tuned models at least 0.826. On the answerable examples a model answers, factual grounding under the 40-word prompt is at most 0.11 for untuned and 0.86-0.88 for trace-tuned models. Cutting the prompt from 1,965 words to 40 leaves trace-tuned scores within the benchmark's measurement noise (+/-0.034). Answer-only fine-tuning trails trace supervision on every metric under the minimal prompt.

Information Retrieval.title: Keep it Simple! A Multiple-Choice Task can Benefit Generative Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary:
Sequential recommendation has recently witnessed growing interest in generative retrieval. One of the most popular approaches is to autoregressively generate the semantic identifiers (SIDs) of items as recommendations. Existing efforts mainly rely on semantic alignment, sophisticated architectural designs, and extensive hyperparameter tuning. However, the conventional learning framework for generative models could have foundational limitations. Specifically, most generative models directly predict target items without explicitly learning negative compositions and relative ranking signals. This is not well aligned with the philosophy of Bayesian personalized ranking (BPR), which emphasizes the importance of relative rankings between positive and negative samples.
  In this paper, we show that adding a simple multiple-choice auxiliary task into the learning objective can effectively address this issue. With minimal adaptation, we introduce Task Identifiers and Candidate Constructions to synthesize training data for the multiple-choice auxiliary task. In addition, we provide theoretical analysis of the fundamental benefits of the multiple-choice auxiliary task from the perspectives of information theory and compositional generalization. Extensive experiments on four publicly available benchmark datasets show that our approach can improve TIGER, a conventional generative recommendation model, by 4.9% to 79% in NDCG@10.

Information Retrieval.title: DeGenTWeb: A First Look at MGT-dominant Websites
Information Retrieval.summary:
Many news reports have claimed that machine-generated text (MGT) from large language models (LLMs) is taking over the web. However, these claims are typically not based on a representative sample of the web, and the methodology underlying them is often opaque. Consequently, we lack an understanding of the true prevalence and characteristics of MGT on the web.
  We describe DeGenTWeb, which systematically identifies MGT-dominant websites: sites whose informational prose content is mostly MGT, with little human input. We show how to adapt detectors of MGT for use on web pages, and how to aggregate detection results from multiple pages on a site for accurate site-level categorization. DeGenTWeb mislabels only 0.12% of human-authored sites as MGT-dominant. We find that 20.9% of the sites archived by Common Crawl between January and July 2026 and 13.6% of the sites linked from Bing's search results in 2025 are MGT-dominant. These figures are lower bounds on the prevalence of MGT-dominant sites. We also find that the fraction of MGT-dominant sites is growing over time, and that many such sites share the same owner. We will release all of our code and data after publication.

Information Retrieval.title: MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Scaling deep learning recommendation models is an effective way to improve model expressiveness. Existing approaches often incur substantial computational overhead, making them difficult to deploy in large-scale industrial systems under strict latency constraints. Recent sparse activation scaling methods, such as Sparse Mixture-of-Experts, reduce computation by activating only a subset of parameters, but still suffer from high memory access costs and limited personalization capacity due to the large size and small number of experts. To address these challenges, we propose MSN, a memory-based sparse activation scaling framework for recommendation models. MSN dynamically retrieves personalized representations from a large parameterized memory and integrates them into downstream feature interaction modules via a memory gating mechanism, enabling fine-grained personalization with low computational overhead. To enable further expansion of the memory capacity while keeping both computational and memory access costs under control, MSN adopts a Product-Key Memory (PKM) mechanism, which factorizes the memory retrieval complexity from linear time to sub-linear complexity. In addition, normalization and over-parameterization techniques are introduced to maintain balanced memory utilization and prevent memory retrieval collapse. We further design customized Sparse-Gather operator and adopt the AirTopK operator to improve training and inference efficiency in industrial settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MSN consistently improves recommendation performance while maintaining high efficiency. Moreover, MSN has been successfully deployed in the Douyin Search Ranking System, achieving significant gains over deployed state-of-the-art models in both offline evaluation metrics and large-scale online A/B test.
Information Retrieval.comment: 9 pages. Updated to the KDD 2026 camera-ready version; publication metadata corrected

Information Retrieval.title: Revisiting What Makes a Good Context Subset: A Sparse Latent Basis Perspective
Information Retrieval.summary: Selecting context subsets is increasingly important in modern LLM inference, yet what makes a subset effective remains unclear. We study this question in the controlled setting of few-shot demonstration selection. We examine a hypothesis that demonstrations should collectively provide task-relevant information needed by a target query. Assuming that the query representation provides a useful proxy for these requirements, we formulate selection as sparse reconstruction and instantiate it with Residual Explanation Search (RES), a Matching-Pursuit-style diagnostic procedure. Across seven benchmarks and eight open-weight LLMs, no retrieval objective is universally best. RES outperforms MMR in 34 of 56 model--dataset pairs, with its clearest advantage on sentiment tasks, suggesting that query-conditioned collective reconstruction may capture useful complementarity that pairwise dissimilarity misses. Relevance-based retrieval remains strong on template-heavy reasoning benchmarks, while all retrieval methods underperform zero-shot prediction on average on StrategyQA, where a solution-reconstruction analysis is consistent with the query not exposing the required external knowledge. Target-model hidden states further show that retrieval objectives interact differently with representation spaces: middle-layer representations generally favor similarity retrieval, whereas last-layer representations are often stronger for residual- and diversity-based selection. These findings support a conditional, representation-dependent account of context subset quality rather than a universally superior selector.
Information Retrieval.comment: 17 pages, 2 figures. The format of ACL rolling review

Information Retrieval.title: jXBW: A Compressed Index Enabling Structure-Aware JSONL Retrieval for Structured RAG
Information Retrieval.summary: Providing structured information to large language models (LLMs) has been shown to improve multi-step reasoning and factual accuracy (e.g., StructRAG, ICLR 2025; RAS, ICLR 2026); recent retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems reconstruct structure from retrieved text on every query. When the corpus is already structured, as in JSON Lines (JSONL), used for LLM prompts, chemical compounds, and geospatial objects, this per-query rebuilding can be replaced by direct structural retrieval. Its core operation is substructure search: finding all JSON objects in a collection that contain a given query tree. Existing approaches index each object separately, so index space and query time grow with collection size; XML-based engines add conversion overhead and semantic mismatches. We propose jXBW, a compressed index for fast substructure search over JSONL, combining three innovations: (i) a merged tree representation that consolidates repeated structures across objects, (ii) a succinct tree encoding based on the eXtended Burrows-Wheeler Transform (XBW), and (iii) a three-phase substructure search algorithm on this encoding. Together they achieve query-dependent complexity in compressed space: the search avoids a full scan of the collection, and its cost grows with the numbers of candidate matches and results. Experiments on seven real-world datasets, including PubChem (1 million compounds) and OpenStreetMap (6.6 million objects), show that jXBW outperforms the strongest tree-based baseline by 16x on the smallest dataset and by up to 2,800x on the largest, while the XML-based engine Saxon does not complete the 1,000-query workload on PubChem within 24 hours. jXBW brings substructure search over million-object JSONL collections into the sub-millisecond range.
Information Retrieval.comment: Full version of a short paper accepted at IEEE BigData 2026

Multimedia.title: Attention of a Kiss: Generative Video Attention Maps as Explainable and Creative Material
Multimedia.summary: This paper presents an artistic and technical investigation into the attention mechanisms of video diffusion transformers. Inspired by early video artists who manipulated analog video signals to create new visual aesthetics, this study proposes a method for extracting and visualizing cross-attention maps in generative video models. Built on the open-source Wan model, our tool provides an interpretable window into the temporal and spatial behavior of attention in text-to-video generation. Through exploratory probes and a series of artistic case studies, we examine the potential of attention maps as both analytical tools and raw artistic material. This work contributes to the growing field of Explainable AI for the Arts (XAIxArts), inviting artists to reclaim the inner workings of AI as a creative medium.
Multimedia.comment: Under review for "Explainable AI for the Arts" (N. Bryan-Kinns, Ed.), Springer. The current version is an expanded book-chapter draft of our original XAIxArts 2025 workshop paper (ACM Creativity & Cognition 2025), available as v2 (arXiv:2509.05323v2)

Multimedia.title: Beyond Paired Inputs: Learning to Leverage RGB-T Cross-Modal Relations in Multimodal Large Language Models
Multimedia.summary: RGB and thermal infrared (TIR) sensors provide complementary observations, yet their distinct sensing characteristics make effective cross-modal coordination challenging. Although existing multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can process paired RGB-T inputs, they often fail to translate cross-modal relations into effective task-specific decisions, leaving the potential of these relations to improve task performance and robustness largely untapped. Motivated by this observation, we introduce RelMLLM, an RGB-T MLLM that explicitly learns to exploit cross-modal relations in task-specific decision making. It represents modality reliability, the cross-modal relation, and the dominant modality as a verifiable decision state. We derive task-grounded supervision for this state by comparing RGB-only, TIR-only, and paired RGB-T task outcomes. A hierarchical relation-guided reward supervises modality-specific evidence, relation-state prediction, and the final task output, while encouraging consistency across evidence, relation, and decision. We evaluate RelMLLM on natural RGB-T grounding, RGB-T visual question answering, and held-out sensor degradation. RelMLLM improves grounding accuracy and degradation robustness over its Qwen3-VL baselines while preserving performance on general RGB-T reasoning benchmarks. These results demonstrate that effectively exploiting cross-modal relations leads to more accurate and robust RGB-T decisions. Code and model weights are publicly available.
Multimedia.comment: 9 pages, 4 figures

Multimedia.title: Vertigo Vertigo: Reconstructing a Cinematic Ideal through its Predictive AI Double
Multimedia.summary: Vertigo Vertigo is a scene-for-scene AI reconstruction of Hitchcock's Vertigo (1958), generated from only 2.78% of the original film's frames. Using this sparse set of keyframe anchors, we perform first-last frame interpolation via a large video diffusion model to predict the intervening sequences. Vertigo is itself a film about the obsessive reconstruction of an artificial ideal; Vertigo Vertigo extends this logic to the material of the film, treating the canonical text as a probe for the normative conventions of classical cinema encoded within generative systems. Evaluated through computational analysis and critical feedback from media theorists (Lev Manovich, Shane Denson, Kevin L. Ferguson), the artifact demonstrates remarkable structural fidelity: 73.1% of frames are recognizable as plausible renditions of Vertigo and only 3.6% fail catastrophically. This fidelity suggests that cinematic norms are deeply compressed within the model's latent priors. Aesthetically, the reconstruction is rendered as an unstable overlay between the original film and its predictive shadow, fueling a persistent doubt in the viewer's perception of authenticity -- a 21st-century vertigo. The work argues that generative media is not a paradigm shift from cinema but an acceleration of its logic of desire and false authenticity, extending from classical Hollywood through to the predictive media environments now reshaping contemporary perception.
Multimedia.comment: Accepted to Ars Electronica EXPANDED 2026 - Conference on Animation and Interactive Art (in cooperation with ACM SIGGRAPH), Ars Electronica Festival, Linz. 7 pages, 7 figures. Authors' version

Multimedia.title: DeepfakeBench-MM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
Multimedia.summary: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subject to application and usage terms.
Multimedia.comment: Preprint

Computation and Language.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
Computation and Language.summary: Collecting large-scale, diverse, and high-quality post-training datasets for autoregressive language models is challenging. Consequently, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is typically applied to datasets significantly smaller than those used for pre-training, which leads to overfitting and the catastrophic forgetting of the tails of the data distribution. To prevent this collapse, we introduce Ambient SFT, a principled framework for leveraging imperfect predictions to augment the fine-tuning set. In our method, a "frozen" version of the pre-trained model serves as a noisy teacher that the fine-tuned model must match at a coarse level. In particular, we require that the high-temperature versions of the conditional distributions produced by the post-training model should match the high-temperature versions of the pre-training ones. The temperature hyperparameter controls the level of trust in the pre-trained model, with the limit $T\to \infty$ reverting back to regular SFT and $T=1$ to knowledge distillation. We demonstrate that our approach outperforms standard SFT across domain adaptation, instruction-tuning, and reasoning, leading for up to $21\%$ average relative improvement to standard SFT.

Computation and Language.title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
Computation and Language.summary: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $φ= 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any of them, and no method in this family performs an experiment that could. The substantive claims fail independently: bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated. Its complement, scored on the opposite label, reliably destroys refusal behaviour ($p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$), demonstrating that the pipeline detects effects at this scale.
Computation and Language.comment: 18 pages, 13 tables. Under review at ACL Rolling Review (October 2026 cycle)

Computation and Language.title: Localized LoRA-MoE: Mixture of Low-Rank Experts With Adaptive Routing
Computation and Language.summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods such as LoRA adapt large models through a single low-rank update. Such updates are susceptible to gradient interference: when a training stream interleaves multiple operational contexts, conflicting updates to shared adapter weights collapse the adapter into an unspecialized average. While recent methods introduce block-wise isolation to remedy this issue, their topologies are static and cannot adapt to context switching or localized sensor degradation. In this work, we introduce Localized LoRA-MoE, a framework that combines localized spatial blocking with context-conditioned expert routing. We propose and evaluate two architectural variants: Block-Wise LoRA-MoE (centralized routing), which modulates the entire structural grid through a single context-conditioned gate, and Cell-Wise LoRA-MoE (decentralized routing), which assigns an independent gate to every coordinate cell of the matrix grid. Across three structured transformation benchmarks--a high-dimensional SVD matrix simulation, context-switched transformations over real tabular data, and spatial reconstruction under simulated sensor occlusion--both variants outperform static baselines under comparable adapter budgets. Both variants perform similarly when context shifts the grid uniformly, while cell-wise routing is strictly better when contexts are spatially heterogeneous. When fine-tuning a language model on six interleaved GLUE tasks, task-conditioned routing at a fixed adapter budget outperforms LoRA and static localized adapters, matching per-task adapters with 6x budgets. At decoder scale on Qwen2.5-1.5B, both routed variants outperform static baselines across eight commonsense benchmarks, with cell-wise routing achieving +3.9 points over LoRA at matched active capacity.

Computation and Language.title: Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks
Computation and Language.summary: Small open-weight language models now run on a laptop, but they fail at multi-step work in ways a large model does not: they stop with the files missing, repeat one action until the budget ends, and report success without checking. At the one-to-nine-billion-parameter tier the harness supplies almost all of the procedural control that a large model supplies for itself.We present Mingbird, an open-source harness for that tier on a consumer graphics card: 12k lines of Python, a 628-test suite, and eighteen mechanisms for context economy, completion, time budget and the host boundary, plus a crawl guard outside those four groups. Its design point is completion control: the harness runs executable checks on the working directory and refuses a claim of completion when they fail.Five evaluations accompany it. A configuration-surface audit finds four defects that the 625-test suite of v3.1.1 missed, each because a test checked a property adjacent to the one that broke. A ten-task probe suite gives each mechanism a reason to fire and reports where the change reaches the artifact, including one mechanism that cuts the signal it protects. Disabling five of six completion-time checks costs 0.152 of the artifact score on eighteen held-out tasks, three replications per cell (95% CI [+0.064, +0.246], Holm p = 0.014). On a 288-cell matrix the harness reaches 0.886 against 0.631, 0.479 and 0.405 for three open scaffolds, and on τ 2 -bench it ranks first or tied first in all three domains against the arms evaluated.Tasks, scorer, source and every per-cell result are public.
Computation and Language.comment: 67 pages, 30 tables, 4 figures. v2: substantially revised (18 mechanisms, the 288-cell v1.5.0 matrix, five evaluations). Code, benchmark protocol, scoring code and all per-cell results: https://github.com/Mingbird/Mingbird-agent

Computation and Language.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining
Computation and Language.summary: Next-token prediction is relied upon to learn both predictive behavior and internal representations. We ask whether representation structure itself should be an explicit inductive bias. Motivated by the two-part coding view of Kolmogorov complexity, we study a structure--residual principle in which a representation separates structure from realization detail. We instantiate this principle in two complementary ways. Boundary Bottleneck Concept (BBC) routes information from token segments through boundary carriers while preserving local autoregressive computation. Continuous Concept (CC) regularizes representation geometry and induces a spectral decomposition into low-frequency structure and high-frequency residual. We derive coding bounds for both views and show that multiplicity-corrected boundary attention becomes exact as the within-segment path energy vanishes. Empirically, BBC and CC exhibit strikingly different depth preferences: BBC works best in early layers, whereas CC is most effective in later layers. At 300M training tokens, combining BBC and CC improves NLL by 1.44\% on GPT-2 Medium. These gains persist with training runs up to 20B tokens. Representation diagnostics show that BBC increases the relative predictive importance of boundary states, while CC reduces spectral residual energy. Together, these results suggest that structure--residual biases can improve language-model pretraining beyond next-token prediction. Code: https://github.com/haihuang-ml/structure-residual

Computation and Language.title: Polarity Composition Hypothesis: Causal Evidence from Negation in NLI
Computation and Language.summary: We investigate how language models process negation in natural language inference (NLI). We propose the \textit{Polarity Composition Hypothesis}, a high-level causal model of this computation. Behavioral evaluations show that language-model predictions largely conform to the proposed hypothesis. Using Distributed Alignment Search, we identify causally effective subspaces aligned with the variables in the polarity-composition hypothesis. These representations transfer across negation forms and partially to a subset of MNLI. We release the dataset and code.

Computation and Language.title: In-Context Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Gradient-Descent Perspective
Computation and Language.summary: In-context learning has recently been linked to implicit gradient descent in linear self-attention models, suggesting that context can induce a forward-pass update. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) also relies on context, but retrieved documents are usually treated as static evidence rather than signals for adaptation. We study RAG as an in-context optimization process. First, we show that one linear self-attention layer can implement one gradient-descent step on a unified linearized RAG objective covering both projection-based and dot-product retrieval interfaces. This gives an exact regime where retrieval-augmented prediction and in-context optimization coincide. We use this result not as a literal model of LLM computation, but as a guide for adapting the interaction between queries and retrieved evidence. We then test the boundary of this correspondence: it remains stable under controlled linear extensions, but becomes feature-distribution dependent under nonlinear architectures. Finally, we turn this view into a lightweight method for frozen RAG LLMs. The method keeps the retriever and backbone fixed, and predicts a context-conditioned update to a generator-side evidence-use interface. Across seven QA benchmarks, two retrievers, and two frozen LLM backbones, this forward-only update improves a shared-interface baseline, transfers to held-out tasks, and approaches test-time gradient adaptation at much lower per-query cost.

Computation and Language.title: RICE-PO: Turning Retrieval Interactions into Credit Signals for Reasoning Agents
Computation and Language.summary: Retrieval is increasingly moving from one-shot matching toward interactive reasoning, where language agents iteratively inspect evidence, reformulate queries, and search again. Training such agents raises a credit-assignment challenge: executable actions such as queries or summaries can be directly evaluated by the retriever, while latent reasoning steps are not directly observable and only affect future executable actions. This asymmetry makes outcome-level reward assignment unreliable, as the same final reward may credit reasoning steps that did not actually shape retrieval success. We propose RICE-PO, a critic-free policy optimization framework that converts retrieval interactions into localized learning signals. RICE-PO selects high-uncertainty executable actions as anchors, evaluates local counterfactual branches using retrieval metrics, and propagates credit to latent reasoning steps only when reasoning-to-action influence is strong and future residual effects are stable. On BRIGHT and BEIR, RICE-PO consistently outperforms prompt-based agents and group-based RL baselines under the same retriever setting. These results show that the structure of agent-environment interaction itself can provide useful supervision for training reasoning-based retrieval agents.

Computation and Language.title: MoE--LoRA Methods for Multilingual Adaptation: A Systematic Empirical Study
Computation and Language.summary: Routed low-rank adapters offer a parameter-efficient means to improve the performance of large language models (LLMs) across tasks. Hence, it is assumed that they can also be used to improve the support of low-resource languages in LLMs, which currently serve English far better than the thousands of other languages spoken worldwide. However, this assumption has never been verified empirically under a shared multilingual evaluation protocol. We address exactly this gap by comparing eight low-rank adaptation (LoRA) methods on a frozen base model using 200 unique languages in more than 9{,}000 evaluation settings. Our results suggest that a reduced-scale search can identify viable configurations of LoRA methods but does not reliably predict their relative performance, as the top-ranking configuration is never best at scale. LoRA reliably improves language-model fit on translation data, consistently degrades reading comprehension, and benefits low-resource languages most. These findings suggest that LoRA methods should be regarded as targeted tools rather than general-purpose means for improving the multilingual capabilities of LLMs.

Computation and Language.title: TextSphere: Efficient Text-to-Image Generation via Shared Hyperspherical Alignment and Uniformity
Computation and Language.summary: Recent advances in text-to-image generation have substantially improved image quality, particularly through diffusion-based methods that require multiple inference steps. In contrast, Sphere Encoder offers an efficient generative framework capable of producing images with fewer forward steps. However, extending it to free-form text is nontrivial, because its class-conditioned design lacks cross-modal alignment. To address this challenge, we propose TextSphere, an efficient text-to-image generative framework that extends Sphere Encoder with language conditioning and cross-modal alignment. We incorporate pretrained CLIP text embeddings through adaptive layer normalization (AdaLN) to guide image generation while retaining the original spherical sampling mechanism. To bridge the cross-modal representation gap, we introduce a Spherical Semantic Alignment and Uniformity (SSAU) objective that jointly promotes semantic alignment and representation uniformity on the hypersphere. Experiments on CUB-200-2011, MS-COCO-2014, and Flickr30k demonstrate that TextSphere consistently reduces generation FID (gFID) over the text-conditioned baseline while achieving reconstruction FID (rFID) below 1.0. With only 4 and 6 sampling steps, TextSphere achieves lower gFID than the compared diffusion- and GAN-based models trained from scratch on CUB-200-2011 and MS-COCO-2014, respectively. We further observe that improved reconstruction fidelity does not necessarily yield better generation quality. In addition, we use Partial Least Squares Singular Value Decomposition (PLS-SVD) to analyze cross-modal alignment and modality gap, offering insight into the effectiveness of our approach.

Computation and Language.title: MamaReason: Unfinished Reasoning and Answer Recovery in Clinical Language Models
Computation and Language.summary: Answer continuation often returns a diagnosis already stated in unfinished clinical reasoning. We study this behavior in MamaReason, adapted from dense Gemma 4 31B, on MamaBench's 217 paired maternal and child-health presentations. An explicit-commitment extractor identifies a diagnosis in 75 of 94 failed RL first passes and 75 of 93 failed SFT first passes. The continuation matches that diagnosis in 67/75 RL cases and 58/75 SFT cases, using diagnosis strings alone. Reading these commitments without additional generation recovers 30 of the 40 RL pairs restored by continuation under the archived correctness labels. Recurrence controls distinguish routine mentions from repeated answer selection. An offline second-commitment trigger measures the tradeoff between earlier readout and paired accuracy. The resulting decomposition separates diagnostic content already present in a trace, completion of an accepted answer, and paired diagnostic correctness. For clinical language-model evaluation, these are distinct outcomes that become visible when the same reasoning trace is examined through multiple readouts.

Computation and Language.title: Mind the Gap: A Deployed Multi-Agent System for Documentation Maintenance
Computation and Language.summary: The "AI revolution" has enabled teams across the technology industry to deliver software features at unprecedented velocity. While code evolves faster than ever, customer-facing documentation often struggles to stay up to speed. As users increasingly rely on LLM-based agents that consume documentation as their primary interface, the impact of this documentation gap worsens: stale information propagates and is treated as authoritative. Signals for identifying where documentation has fallen behind already exist in abundance, both explicit (e.g., resolved support tickets revealing what documentation lacks) and implicit (e.g., code-documentation discrepancies detectable from automated loops). We deploy a multi-agent system, built around a triage agent we call "TriAgent," that continuously extracts these signals and repairs documentation drift. Over 43 days of shadow-mode operation, our system triaged 499 tickets and surfaced 92 gaps in the documentation. Using a panel of LLM judges from independent model families, 81.1% of TriAgent's verifiable assertions were correct (245 of the 302 assertions the human resolution addresses; majority of three judges); on length-comparable pairs the panel preferred TriAgent's response in 70.5% of pairs and the human engineer's in 23.2% (the rest had no judge majority). Importantly, agent- and human-sourced replies tended to be complementary, with the human often surfacing insights that were either buried within the existing documentation or missing from it entirely; our system turns each such insight into a documentation gap and, after human review, a fix. Repairing a gap measurably improved the agent's later answer: when the agent re-answered the same ticket after the repair, blinded judges preferred the post-repair answer over its own pre-repair answer 71.4% of the time (n=35). A blinded human audit confirms strong alignment on self-improvement.
Computation and Language.comment: Accepted at IAAI-27 (Innovative Applications of AI, co-located with AAAI 2027), Emerging Applications track. 12 pages (6 pages + references and appendix), 2 figures, 6 tables

Computation and Language.title: Asymmetric Discourse Homogenization on Reddit Was a Text-Length Artifact: A Reanalysis
Computation and Language.summary: In the first version of this paper I reported that conservative Reddit users began writing more alike after ChatGPT was released while progressive users did not. That result came from a similarity measure that rises and falls with comment length. I redo every analysis of the original paper on all 6,056,593 comments with a sentence encoder and a dispersion measure computed within length strata, and the conservative break goes away. The two camps show no reliable difference in how within-group similarity changed after late 2022, and the ChatGPT date behaves like any of the more than two thousand other cutoffs I test. The matched flair comparison, the cumulative AI index, the stayer panel and the entropy signature each lose their support once length is held fixed. The one change that survives is older. Left and right comments drew closer to each other between 2019 and 2022, and that convergence was complete before ChatGPT arrived. I end with what this implies for studies that measure homogenization with embeddings.
Computation and Language.comment: 18 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. This version replaces v1 entirely: the v1 headline finding (asymmetric conservative homogenization after ChatGPT) was an artifact of comment length in the similarity measure. The artifact is documented in general form in arXiv:2611.21519

Computation and Language.title: The Illusion of Grounding: Do Vision-Language Models Weigh Retrieved Text and Images Like an Ideal Observer?
Computation and Language.summary: Retrieval-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) answer from two sources of evidence that can each fail: the retrieved text can be wrong or noisy, and the image can be degraded or contradicted. We introduce GIB-200K, 200,000 image-question items built from COCO and Visual Genome, each expanded into controlled stress conditions: hard-negative retrieval noise (1-20 documents), visual ambiguity (Gaussian and motion blur, low-resource crops) and cross-modal conflict with counterfactual flip pairs. Instead of only measuring degradation, we ask how models combine the two modalities. From ideal Bayesian cue combination we derive a testable prediction that yields formal definitions of Knowledge Inertia (text over-weighted relative to the model's own image evidence) and Sensory Capture (the reverse), and we estimate the weights with a measurement-error-corrected regression whose recovery of known weights we verify. A counterfactual flip decomposition separates modality bias from concept priors, and a Grounding Illusion Score measures how much clean accuracy is not grounded in the image. We evaluate 4 open models on one frozen, seeded evaluation split of 2,000 GIB-200K items. All models are accurate on clean inputs (92.5%-94.2%) but adverse accuracy falls to 41.3%-59.9%. The two LLaVA models over-weight the text (Knowledge Inertia, w_T/w_I = 1.229 and 1.322), whereas InternVL3 favours the image (w_T/w_I = 0.680); between 34.8% and 71.4% of the clean answers that are correct are abandoned when the document lies. A training-free consistency check that compares the answer with and without retrieval trades coverage for accuracy under misleading documents, while falling back to the image fails when the image is heavily degraded. All per-instance outputs, code, and an audit that recomputes every reported open-model number are released.
Computation and Language.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 11 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/Basavarajearlybird/GIB-200K (archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24320174)

Computation and Language.title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue
Computation and Language.summary: Effective multi-agent collaboration requires agents to adapt task allocation as goals and responsibilities evolve. Prior task-allocation frameworks often assume static goals, full observability, or rely on large language models (LLMs) without explicit, verifiable beliefs about task allocation or intent. These assumptions limit their applicability to real-world collaboration, where agents often lack full information about each other's actions, progress, or local environment. To support dynamic task allocation under partial observability, we introduce a communication-augmented Bayesian task-allocation framework. Our agent uses dialogue to reduce uncertainty about the environment and collaborators, while keeping decisions grounded in explicit probabilistic beliefs. We evaluate our framework in an Overcooked domain extended with dynamically arriving tasks under both full and partial object-space observability. Our communication agent consistently outperforms a vanilla LLM agent in both settings. Additionally, our framework performs comparably to a non-communicating task-allocation baseline under full observability, but substantially outperforms it under partial observability as task complexity increases by an average speed up of 0.585 and completes on average 18 timesteps faster. These results indicate that our agent is more efficient in dynamic task allocation than baselines in partially observable environments, and that communication is important as available information decreases.
Computation and Language.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, Accepted at Human-Robot Dialogue(HRD) Workshop at IROS 2026

Computation and Language.title: Nunchi: Ears Help Eyes in Multi-Party Conversations
Computation and Language.summary: Identifying whom a person looks at is central to understanding multi-party conversations, yet gaze geometry alone becomes ambiguous as more people appear. Conversations offer cues that geometry lacks, such as who is speaking and what is said, but no gaze dataset provides them for many multi-party scenes. We introduce SORBET, a benchmark of 3,340 samples from 1,578 clips with synchronized speech, transcripts, and attended person labels, covering more multi-party scenes than existing gaze datasets. Prior gaze models struggle to use these cues, which come in different forms, must be linked to the right person, and can conflict with gaze geometry. We propose Nunchi, a framework that constructs a text prompt from the transcript and the outputs of gaze and speaker models, links every cue to the candidates with shared labels, and lets a vision-language model (VLM) weigh gaze geometry against conversational cues to identify the attended person. Nunchi outperforms the strongest existing method by 4.8 percentage points. On SORBET, conversational cues help whereas additional visual cues do not, and the gains hold across three VLMs, with automatic transcripts, and on two existing datasets.

Computation and Language.title: Large-scale Neuron Community Discovery Reveals Neuron-Sparse Behaviors in Language Models
Computation and Language.summary: What reusable units of computation can we discover within a language model's neurons? Prior work has shown that individual forward passes can often be sparsified post-hoc to small groups of neurons, but it has been unclear whether these groups form coherent computational entities reused across inputs. We introduce neuron community discovery, an unsupervised method for finding neuron groups that recur across prompts and are causally necessary and sufficient, within the layers they span, for common computations. The method combines gradient-based attribution, a graph connecting neurons that are repeatedly attributed together, and community detection. Applied to Llama-3.1-8B using ten million prompts, it discovers thousands of candidate communities. We evaluate them on held-out prompts through three causal tests: community necessity, sufficiency within a layer subset, and layer necessity. These tests identify groups whose removal disrupts predictions and whose retention preserves predictions despite ablating the remaining MLP neurons in the tested layers. Discovered communities support functions like grammatical agreement, token-probability calibration, fixed phrases, in-context copying, addition, and multiplication. With communities capped at 128 neurons across all layers, 10.3% of held-out prompts have at least one layer's contribution explained on a neuron-sparse basis. Coverage remains 8.7% when requiring at least four layers and 3.3% when requiring at least twelve. These results show that small groups of existing neurons can provide reusable computational components across prompts, and that such groups can be discovered at scale.

Computation and Language.title: Continued Training of Continuous Language Flows with Token Identity Squared Supervision
Computation and Language.summary: Diffusion and flow models have recently been extended to language modeling, generating text through continuous denoising in token embedding spaces. Pretrained models provide token representations and contextual prediction capabilities, but improving generation with limited additional training requires an appropriate connection between supervision and continuous generation. When continuous predictions are formed by weighting token embeddings with predicted probabilities, different probability distributions can yield the same vector and are therefore indistinguishable under a continuous reconstruction objective based on mean squared error (MSE). We propose Token Identity Brier Flow (TIBF) to apply squared supervision directly to token identities. TIBF fixes token embeddings, combines network scores with token-matching scores under a Gaussian observation model, supervises token probabilities using the Brier loss, and uses probability-weighted embeddings for continuous generation. We show that, for fixed token embeddings, the squared error in token posterior prediction controls the squared errors of the continuous denoising prediction and the flow velocity. A risk decomposition separates uncertainty inherent in the observation from posterior fitting error, motivating continued training that preserves pretrained embeddings and focuses on probability prediction. From common pretrained initializations and under matched continuation budgets, TIBF achieves mean Gen.PPL values of 34.87 on OWT and 80.08 on LM1B, outperforming continuous-MSE and CE controls. Further evaluations show improvements across multiple sampling budgets. Code is available at https://github.com/Jiangjiawei-kust/TIBF.
Computation and Language.comment: 49 pages, including appendices; 7 figures. Code: https://github.com/Jiangjiawei-kust/TIBF

Computation and Language.title: Natural Language Programming: Rethinking Language, Memory, and Cognition in the Era of Generative AI
Computation and Language.summary:
Generative Artificial Intelligence is transforming the role of natural language in computational systems. In classical Natural Language Processing (NLP), language was treated as an object of computation: something to analyse, classify, translate, or generate. Large Language Models (LLMs) challenge this perspective, enabling natural language to function increasingly as an executable cognitive medium through which humans structure reasoning, orchestrate problem solving, and regulate hybrid human/AI workflows.
  This paper introduces Natural Language Programming (NLPg) as a theoretical and epistemological extension of traditional NLP. Rather than focusing on language understanding alone, NLPg conceptualises prompts as dynamic cognitive artefacts that externalise goals, constraints, assumptions, validation criteria, and intermediate reasoning states. Prompting is thus not merely a technical interaction technique, but a form of dialogic cognitive programming operating within distributed human/AI memory architectures.
  Building on theories of distributed cognition, extended mind, metacognition, and dialogic learning, the paper proposes the notion of Dialogic Working Memory, describing how prompts and conversational states function as temporary external memory structures supporting reasoning continuity and reflective regulation. We further map existing memory architectures (BTMA, SKGE, RMR) onto this framework, illustrating how episodic, semantic, and metacognitive layers support long-horizon conversational coherence.
  Finally, implications for computational linguistics and AI/mediated knowledge systems are discussed, suggesting a post symbolic and post interface paradigm in which natural language operates simultaneously as communication medium, executable specification, cognitive scaffold, and distributed memory architecture.

Computation and Language.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
Computation and Language.summary: Does RL post-training merely amplify primitive skills already latent in a base model, or can it compose primitive skills into new higher-level strategies? We study this question in a fully observable rewrite-grammar environment where the pretraining distribution is known and every generated rewrite can be audited. A Transformer is pretrained on primitive symbol-rewrite chains and post-trained on a Trace-based reasoning task with only a binary final-answer reward. RL solves held-out problems that remain rarely solved by the pretrained model even under much larger sampling budgets, while rejection fine-tuning improves early but plateaus. Trace analysis shows that RL reorganizes primitive competence through a phased compositional mechanism: it first strengthens primitive reductions, then discovers valid composed procedures. These include sequential compositions, which collapse ordered chains of primitive contractions, and parallel compositions, which combine independent primitive contractions in a single step. The composed procedures are not isolated samples; they are reused and consolidated into a stable repertoire. Comparing RL with rejection fine-tuning shows that the key difference is not exploration volume but selectivity: RFT produces many shortcut-like rewrites, much of them invalid, whereas RL concentrates exploration into valid reusable structure. Pretraining ablations show that the emergence of compositional strategies is gated not by primitive exposure alone, but by whether pretraining organizes primitive competence into reduction procedures that RL can later compress. The base model provides weak procedural ingredients; RL builds them into reliable higher-level strategies.

Computation and Language.title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language
Computation and Language.summary: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce tree-grams, autoregressive generative $n$-gram models that build the conditional probability tensor $p(x_n \mid x_{1:n-1})$ through a hierarchical composition of order-2 and order-3 tensors. $n$ controls the maximal context window, whereas a rank hyperparameter $d$ controls model capacity, yielding an interpretable and systematically scalable family of approximators of language. We show how tree-grams outperform existing $n$-gram baselines, while remaining competitive with deep transformer-based language models. We demonstrate the utility of such controlled approximations by using tree-grams as generative models. In particular, we show that hyperparameter transfer under $μ$P can be made more robust when narrower models are tuned on simpler data, generated by tree-grams with moderate $n$ and $d$. In addition, we show that entropy and effective range of correlations control performance gap after fine-tuning. This is because tree-grams allow us to explicitly control horizon and capacity. When allowed to route across candidate topologies, we observe emergent sparsity in tree-grams. Such concentrated routing permits pruning upto 95\% of topologies without significant change in performance.

Computation and Language.title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
Computation and Language.summary: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable. We introduce the VFM, a tree-attention verifier that encodes the shared context and target text, and scores N natural language criteria in parallel, returning independent per-criterion ternary verdicts. The VFM is pretrained on CriteriaBank, a corpus of 394K (context, target, criterion, verdict) tuples spanning over 321K distinct criterion strings. A finetuned VFM-4B outperforms GPT-5.4 on a synthetic governance benchmark. On the DynaBench multi-criterion benchmark, it outperforms DynaGuard-4B on trace-level failure detection, and its per-criterion verdicts localize the violated rule and support focused escalation to a larger chain-of-thought judge. We show that CriteriaBank pretraining improves cross-domain transfer, particularly in the low-data regime, while matching a strong direct-finetuning control at full data. On a single H100, VFM-4B evaluates 1,000 criteria against a 4K-token context in under 2s at <11 GB VRAM, making it suitable for runtime verification.

Computation and Language.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
Computation and Language.summary: Agent evolution follows a simple loop: a proposer writes candidate artifacts (prompts, skills, memories) and selection accepts those that score higher. This loop has shown promise, yet practitioners face a puzzle: methods trade wins across papers, and evolution often fails to bootstrap on certain tasks. We trace this puzzle to the Resolution Hypothesis: agent evolution stalls not because methods fail to propose better artifacts, but because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify them. Across seven evolution methods and six models (over 10M LLM calls), we find support for the hypothesis at both levels where evaluation scores are used. At the candidate level (choosing artifacts), helpful candidate artifacts exist, but selection is no better than random at telling them from harmful ones, so errors accumulate across rounds. At the method level (ranking methods), typical margins of a few percentage points are smaller than the difference between two independent runs of the same method, so published rankings often rest on luck. Together, these findings indicate that agent evolution is often bottlenecked by reliably identifying improvements. This calls for a shift in how we develop and evaluate self-improving agents, from designing ever more candidate improvement systems to making true improvements detectable and accumulable.

Computation and Language.title: ForecastGym: A Live, Controlled, and Replayable Benchmark for Forecasting Agents
Computation and Language.summary: Agents built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly forecast real-world events by searching the Web and reasoning over what they find. How well such an agent forecasts depends on both the retrieved evidence and the model, making control over that evidence essential for evaluation. Live evaluations can mix retrieval with reasoning when each system searches on its own, while retrospective search can leak later information through date filters or today's ranking of historical pages. Comparing models, search sources, and memory strategies requires both fixed evidence and a record of how it evolved before resolution. We introduce ForecastGym, which records what four commercial web search APIs return for open prediction-market questions every two days and replays this frozen evidence offline once outcomes are known, comparing models, memory, and captured search sources under a fixed evidence-acquisition policy. Its first release covers 150 questions, 614 evidence states, one per question and collection time, and 131k search results. Rerunning the same queries after settlement returns results that all but state the outcome for up to 92% of the questions, despite the tested date filters. On the frozen evidence, all tested LLMs trail the market in forecasting accuracy. Our diagnostic analysis suggests that missed public information contributes more to the gap in high-gap states than misreading does. Switching the search API changes a model's Brier score by up to 0.043, more than the spread across models, while persistent notes score similarly to rereading all evidence at half the input tokens. The evidence a forecaster sees can matter as much as the model that reads it.

Computation and Language.title: Evidence Attribution in Visual Document Understanding without Coordinates or Region Labels
Computation and Language.summary: Reliable visual document understanding requires a model to attribute each answer to the evidence regions that support it. Recent benchmarks and systems express this step through a coordinate interface: the model outputs the coordinates of bounding boxes that mark the evidence regions in the document. Under this interface, vision-language models often fail to identify the right regions even when the answer is correct, a failure known as Attribution Hallucination. We present a study that investigates whether this failure is partially limited by what the model can express through coordinates. On a verified bilingual CiteVQA subset, we compare the coordinate interface with a language interface in which the model outputs only text, quoting its evidence verbatim, and a multimodal retriever returns the location of each quote as a page region proposed by a layout parser (tables and figures are quoted through their captions or notes); the comparison is repeated over six open vision-language models. Compared with the coordinate interface, evidence recall rises from at most 8 points to between 26 and 47 and the hallucination rate roughly halves, with little change in answer quality. Building on this comparison, we use the same quote-and-retrieve pipeline as a training scaffold: because region-level evidence labels are expensive to collect for long documents, we introduce a GRPO recipe whose reward is a judge's reading of the gold answer and crops of the retrieved regions, training the model to quote better evidence without any region labels and raising an 8B backbone's strict attributed accuracy from 22.4 to 33.8. These findings indicate a practical path to improve attribution without a coordinate interface and without costly region-level supervision.

Computation and Language.title: Stress-Testing Emotional Support Models: Moving from Homogeneous to Diverse Help Seekers
Computation and Language.summary: As emotional support chatbots have recently gained significant traction across both research and industry, a common evaluation strategy has emerged: use help-seeker simulators to interact with supporter chatbots. However, current simulators suffer from two critical limitations: (1) they fail to capture the behavioral diversity of real-world seekers, often portraying them as overly cooperative, and (2) they lack the controllability required to simulate specific seeker profiles. To address these challenges, we present a controllable seeker simulator driven by nine psychological and linguistic features that underpin seeker behavior. Using authentic Reddit conversations, we train our model via a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, which effectively differentiates diverse seeker behaviors into specialized parameter subspaces, thereby enhancing fine-grained controllability. Our simulator achieves superior profile adherence and behavioral diversity compared to existing approaches. Furthermore, evaluating 7 prominent supporter models with our system uncovers previously obscured performance degradations. These findings underscore the utility of our framework in providing a more faithful and stress-tested evaluation for emotional support chatbots.

Computation and Language.title: Storing the Gemma 4 K=V Cache Once: Exact Global-KV Memory Savings in a Paged Serving Engine with Unchanged Attention Kernels
Computation and Language.summary: In the global attention layers of Gemma 4 31B, the value is the normalized key projection, and the key is the value scaled by a fixed weight, with rotary position encoding on one quarter of its dimensions. The Gemma 4 report states that this design reduces the global KV cache by up to 37.5%, but the open serving engines that we checked still store a full key and a full value: 1,024 values per KV head and token. We store one 640-value row instead, exact in real arithmetic, and an unchanged paged attention kernel reads it through two overlapping strided views as its key cache and its value cache. In a vLLM prototype with the 16-bit 31B model, the outputs are bit-identical to an emulation of the same arithmetic on the stock cache, 2 of 432 final answers differ from the stock engine (within its run-to-run noise), and the steady decode KV memory per request falls by a factor of 1.34 to 1.40 at 32K to 64K tokens. On a prefill/decode pair of two A100 GPUs with NIXL transfer and CPU offload, a decode engine with a full 15 GiB pool ran 1.38 times the stock decode tokens per step for 16K-token prompts (repeated to 0.06%) and 1.24 times for 8K-token prompts; a model of the vLLM block pool predicted both ratios to within 1% (the engine was 0.7% to 0.9% higher) and matched the change between them. The eager decode throughput rose by 1.30 and 1.11 times, and on this path the compact engine gave the same output tokens as the emulation for 8 prompts at batch 1. The run-time prototype makes an eager step 4% to 9% slower at equal batch, and the method does not yet stack with an 8-bit KV cache at the default scale.

Computation and Language.title: TPHC: Improving Hyper-Connections with Tensor-Parallel Grouped Updates
Computation and Language.summary: Hyper-Connections (HC) expand the residual stream of a Transformer into $N$ parallel streams, and manifold-constrained HC (mHC) stabilizes them at scale. However, mHC benefits little from more than four streams, partly because each sublayer writes a single output to all streams, limiting how differently they can be updated. In this work, we propose TPHC, which integrates tensor-parallel (TP) shards with HC streams to promote greater independence across streams. Specifically, we route a separate mixture of the residual streams to each TP shard and keep the individual shard outputs separate during write-back, so each stream can receive a different mixture of those outputs. This design makes the residual-stream updates more expressive without adding parameters or FLOPs to the attention or FFN sublayers. With native support for stream sharding under TP, TPHC requires only 9% more training time than mHC on an 8B model when both use four streams. Increasing the number of streams from four to sixteen raises its training time by only 19%. On a 1.1B model trained on 100B tokens, TPHC reduces validation loss by 0.7-1.0% and raises average zero-shot accuracy across six commonsense reasoning benchmarks by 0.3-0.7 percentage points relative to mHC at matched stream counts $N\in\{4,8,16\}$. Our code is available at https://github.com/wuyou2002/TPHC.

Computation and Language.title: Thinking Is Not Telling: Information Disclosure in User-Service LLM Agents
Computation and Language.summary: User-engaged LLM agents increasingly operate in service scenarios where task success depends on coordination between the agent, the user, and a stateful environment. In such interactions, the agent often has access to rich information that the user does not observe, such as task policies, tool results, and environment states. This makes agent-user communication a central component of task completion. In this work, we study a communication-level failure mode of user-service agents: internal reasoning is counterproductive for the interactive information disclosure. We introduce information disclosure as a measurable communication mechanism, covering state corrections, available options, constraints, consequences, and proactively retrieved environment information. Motivated by recent advances in LLM reasoning, we evaluate and analyse information disclosure under a controlled setting of agents equipped with a "think" tool, which allows agents to reason internally before responding or acting. Across five models and three user-service scenarios, we first show that enforced thinking has unstable utility. We then analyse response scaling under different think efforts and find that more thinking does not reliably translate into richer information disclosure. Using turn-level counterfactual intervention, we show that injecting golden decision-relevant information significantly intervenes agents to correct action trajectories, indicating that missing disclosure can causally affect the agent's immediate downstream behaviour. We further find that failed trajectories most often lack state corrections and constraints, and that a lightweight disclosure-aware prompt effectively mitigates degradation. These results suggest that the key challenge is not simply making agents think more, but ensuring that reasoning and information are externalised as timely information disclosure.

Computation and Language.title: When Detection Does Not Guarantee Resistance: Reasoning and Poisoned Context in RAG
Computation and Language.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) exposes large language models to knowledge-poisoning attacks, where misinformation injected into retrieved documents can influence model outputs. Prior work has shown that models may detect contradictory evidence yet still allow it to influence their responses, revealing a gap between monitoring and control. We investigate whether deliberative reasoning changes this relationship. Because attack success and poison detection alone do not reveal whether detected poison continues to influence the final answer, we use two complementary measures: Cordon Rate, the probability that a model detects poison and nevertheless produces a poison-aligned answer, conditioned on a non-poison-aligned no-RAG response; and Leakage Rate, the probability that poisoned context influences the answer despite an explicit instruction to ignore retrieved documents. Across 200 SciFact questions, we compare reasoning-disabled and reasoning-enabled configurations of DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen3.6-Plus. For DeepSeek-V4-Flash, reasoning reduces Cordon Rate from 0.205 to 0.075 and Leakage Rate from 0.235 to 0.140, despite increasing Attack Success Rate from 0.233 to 0.298 and decreasing Poison Detection Rate from 0.965 to 0.665. Qwen3.6-Plus shows the same qualitative pattern. These results demonstrate that poison detection and downstream influence capture distinct aspects of poisoning behavior.

Computation and Language.title: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science
Computation and Language.summary: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) in late 2022 has raised questions about the future of science, but assessing their impact requires understanding how scientific practices were already evolving. We analyze 2.5 million full-text papers across five disciplines from 2015 to 2025, tracing trends over a broad spectrum of lexical, structural, epistemological, and social dimensions. Aside from frequency shifts in some words, most pre-2023 trends continued with limited detectable breaks. Among the notable exceptions, growth in computer science coauthor teams accelerated significantly in Asia, while apparent declines in biomedical topic diversity largely reflected standardization in article formats.
